response:
All measurements, the fix, and both falsifier runs are complete. Final report.

---

## verdict

**RECORDED ONLY** — for `entry["severity"]`, the model-asserted scalar, which is the only thing this codebase currently calls severity. It already reaches the gate through the frozen 0.7 CRITICAL cut and must not reach it a second way. The quantity the founder *defines* — flaw-survival probability after n passes — is a different object, `R_k`, already fundamental to the model, and for that object the destination is **GATES CONVERGENCE (added condition)** — but it is **not implementable as a gate today**, because its inputs do not yet vary with the question (evidence below). No part of this demotes gamma: the two-sided gate is untouched; an `R_k` bound would be a fourth conjunct beside (a) gamma_critical ≥ θ, (b) K zero-critical rounds, (c) A4/not-contested — never a substitute.

## definition

Two load-bearing quantities are currently sharing one word, and his definition picks out exactly one of them:

1. **His definition is `R_k`, verbatim.** `docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md` §1: *"the posterior probability that a flaw of class k remains after n passes that found nothing"* = R = π·m/((1−π)+π·m), m=(1−q)^n. His "complexity of the topic" is π_risk,k (prior flaw rate); his "confidence one can derive" is q (detection power). Computed per entry as `sk_result.R_new` via `compute_rk_with_eta_channel`; carried per flaw class per run since the 2026-10-31 `sk_carry_rk_across_rounds` repair. **Read by no gate.**
2. **`entry["severity"]`** is materiality — consequence-if-real, per the "Objective and Diminishing Returns" directive ("Severity is materiality"). No n, no prior, no detection rate. The 0.7 cut applies to this one.

They are not the same, and the archive says so by execution: over 1,252 paired entries, R_new vs severity Spearman **−0.141** (p=5.7×10⁻⁷), Kendall −0.107 (p=8.2×10⁻⁷). The quantities *anti*-correlate.

## boundaries

- **Asserted severity:** [0,1], cut frozen at 0.7 (pre-registered 2026-05-18; founder ruling: moving it after results is "the single largest cooking vector" — and there is no natural break there: 401 findings sit exactly on 0.70). Stays.
- **R_k as a future gate term:** the bound is *derived, not chosen*, which is what "estimable from a run" means in his units. The inversion exists in closed form (SymPy, this session's run of `scripts/his_severity_definition_is_the_models_own_quantity_2026-10-31.py`): n(R_t) = log[R_t(1−π)/(π(1−R_t))]/log(1−q) — so a pre-registered bound is "the R_k that the estimated (π_k, q) imply after the budgeted pass count," per class. What sets the inputs: **q** from planted-defect detection rates where a seeded control arm exists (exp40 baseline / sim45 canary); **π_k** from archive class-level confirmed-flaw frequencies; default 0.5 only where unknown, stated. Until those are estimated per run, any numeric bound is a chosen constant — exactly the 0.7-everywhere failure he charges.
- His worked contrast, computed and second-checked: R after 6 passes is 3.19×10⁻¹⁰ for (π=0.02, q=0.95) vs 0.8687 for (π=0.9, q=0.05) — ratio **2.72×10⁹** (SymPy+mpmath+NumPy agree; Wolfram Language, local kernel: `{0.8686944966, 3.1888e-10, 2.7242e9}`). A single fixed cut across both is meaningless, in numbers.

## comparability (Q3)

`R_k` needs **no external normalisation**: difficulty enters inside Bayes' formula through (π_k, q). But that is conditional on those inputs varying — and today they do not: `R_old` = 0.500000 in all 1,252 archived entries (distinct count 1), `R_new` spans only [0.3667, 0.5] with 59.3% exactly at 0.3667 (Wilson [0.566, 0.620]) because the recursion re-initialised every round. So archived R_k values are "risk after one pass from a fixed prior" — comparable only because constant, which is vacuous. Asserted severity is **not** on a common scale across experiments and nothing in the harness can normalise it today. Available difficulty observables: γ itself (the Duane slope is already computed per run and is difficulty-sensitive), planted-detection rate on control arms, rounds-to-convergence. The inter-assessor spread does **not** qualify (next section). An answer setting bounds without this is Q2 for one experiment only — agreed.

## instrument_results

1. **Spread.** `python3 scripts/is_severity_noise_or_disagreement_2026-10-19.py`: 152 entries (brief said 147 — archive grew), median **0.1450**, mean **0.1810** (brief: 0.12 / 0.18 — mean matches, midpoint now higher); 71.7% of spreads wider than the 0.09 decision band. Consistent with his definition *in principle*, but see refutation 3: by execution it is indistinguishable from a shared noise floor, so it is currently evidence for a combination rule, not a difficulty signal.
2. **Nothing combines.** Same run: kept value equals median in 21.1%, mean 11.2%, min 30.3%, max 38.8%, and lies **outside [min,max] in 35 of 152 = 23.03%, Wilson [17.05%, 30.33%]** — matches the brief's "35 cases, 18–31%". Established by execution.
3. **0.7 provenance/proxy.** `python3 scripts/the_severity_proxy_was_never_tested_2026-10-28.py`: kappa −0.022688, power 0.1442 against the strong hypothesis — the audit is UNINFORMATIVE, confirmed; 86.7% of 3,256 entries (counts grew from the brief's 3,237) classified at severities the audit never examined; 79.6% of 1,420 CRITICAL calls above the band. **What would settle it:** the already-costed 63-item full-range blind adjudication (simulated power 0.9193); founder-labelled, no model can supply it. **My Q1 answer does not depend on it** — it rests on post-merge untraceability and on R_k being the right gate quantity; the adjudication decides only whether the existing 0.7 cut tracks the rubric.
4. **The instruments.** Executed directly: spec off (default) → `effective_severity` returns asserted (0.8 for all verdicts); after `wire_module_mirrors(severity_spec_enabled=True)` → CONFIRMED 0.8, REFUTED **0.0** (annihilation property), unresolved 0.4. A distribution-valued severity breaks immediately: `TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'list'` — plus every `>= CRITICAL_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD` comparison in `_settled_novelty_series` / `unverified_critical_count` / `_apply_severity_calibration`, and the archive schema.

**Gate inertness test (refutation 1, against the archive):** 41 runs carry R_new; 13 converged via CRITICAL_QUIESCENCE. An added condition max R_new ≤ B flips 13/13 at B=0.30, 10/13 at 0.3667, 4/13 at 0.40, **0/13 at ≥0.45** — and max R_new does not separate converged from non-converged runs (Mann-Whitney p=0.328). So a severity term in the gate today is either inert or flips runs on a quantity carrying no convergence signal. Both fail the additive standard. This is why the verdict is recorded-only *now*, gate *after* carry + estimated (π_k, q) produce varying R_k.

## fix

`bench/reference_runner_v3.py` (sandbox tree, real path), 4 edits, compiles:
- `combine_independent_severities(values)` — pure median combiner, defined above `FindingRegistry`, importable by archive scripts.
- `FindingRegistry.record_codiscovery(..., severity: Optional[float] = None)` — records the co-discoverer's own severity in the codiscovery record and writes `entry["severity_combined"]` = median of all recorded assessments. `entry["severity"]` — the gate input — untouched: byte-identical convergence behaviour; the combined figure reaches archived reports through the existing registry dump.
- Caller wired at the triage loop: `severity=getattr(_tr.finding, "severity", None)`.
- `bench/tests/test_codiscovery_records_severity_2026-10-31.py` executes it.

Median chosen because it is inside [min,max] by construction — the 23% outside-range defect cannot recur — robust to one outlier, and equals the mean at n=2. Simplest sufficient; nothing composed, nothing removed.

## falsifier

`python3 bench/tests/test_codiscovery_records_severity_2026-10-31.py` — imports the real `FindingRegistry`/`Finding`. **Pre-fix:** `FALSIFIED: record_codiscovery takes no severity...`, AssertionError, exit 1. **Post-fix:** clean exit, combined = 0.65 = median(0.5, 0.8), third assessor → 0.8, gate input unchanged. Regression: `pytest` over this file + the 3 existing codiscovery test files: **78 passed**.

## refutation_condition

1. If a future measurement shows an R_k-bound added to the gate changes archived outcomes *correctly* (separates good from bad convergences, Mann-Whitney significant), my "not yet" is overturned — gate it then. Tested: today it does not (p=0.328).
2. If (π_k, q) prove estimable per run today from existing artefacts to better than the 0.5 default, "difficulty is not measurable here" weakens and the gate term becomes buildable now. Partially true already: q is estimable *only* on planted-control arms.
3. If, with more data, exactly-2-assessor spreads differ by run (Kruskal-Wallis significant), the spread is genuine per-question uncertainty, strengthening his confidence reading. Tested: p=0.717 over 12 runs / 98 pairs — currently a shared noise floor, which argues for the combination rule I shipped and against gating on spread. Note the uncontrolled correlations (spread vs rounds_run ρ=+0.41, p=0.003) are a sample-size artefact: range grows with assessment count.
4. If the 63-item full-range adjudication shows the 0.7 proxy contradicts the rubric, the CRITICAL channel itself (the one place severity gates today) needs repair — that would not reverse this verdict but would dominate it in importance.

## strongest_disagreement

The brief's premise 2 — and his definition — quietly collapses two load-bearing quantities into one word. Flaw-survival probability (R_k) and consequence-if-shipped (materiality, the §10/"Objective" sense of severity) are orthogonal: a boring off-by-one is trivially caught (low R_k) and still critical (high materiality); the archive shows the two recorded quantities *anti*-correlate (Spearman −0.141, p=5.7×10⁻⁷). Renaming R_k "severity" and letting it absorb the CRITICAL cut would break the materiality machinery the convergence objective depends on. His quantity is real, already in the model, and should eventually gate — *as R_k, under its own name*. Secondary disagreement: the brief's instrument figures (147 cases, 0.12 midpoint, 3,237 entries, 1,119/1,408) are stale against the current archive (152, 0.145, 3,256, ~1,130/1,420); same phenomena, moved counts.

## termination

5 passes: (1) gate + instrument reading; (2) the 4 required instruments executed; (3) archive replay — gate-inertness sweep and spread-difficulty correlation; (4) exactly-2-assessor control, which *reversed* pass 3's correlation finding (last substantive revision); (5) fix, falsifier pre/post, 78-test regression, Wolfram second check. Pass 5 added confirmations only — no new above-threshold finding. Converged; stopping.
